answer: A network can require unpredictable live presence: at random times, each identity must join a short live session and answer a fresh prompt in real time, like an ivory tower that only opens its gate when called. A vine of a thousand fake identities strangles itself, because one operator can attend only one session at a time — a reef of simultaneous demands no single person can cross. Each extra identity costs another human's undivided minutes, a cost that cannot be shared, queued, or run in parallel.
